description: 3-6 traction-slip events on ONE bogie: low-adhesion patch + anti-slip control (cutoff saw-tooth or creep plateau); the wheel over-reads by ~5-30 % for 1-10 s. Front/rear mismatch reveals it.

Slip on BOTH bogies at once (wet rail) or with a spatial lag (contamination patch passed first by the front, then by the rear bogie). Front/rear consistency no longer reveals the fault; only the notch->acceleration model / acceleration plausibility can.
Modern slip-regulating traction control: both or one wheel held 5-15 % above vehicle speed for 4-10 s as a smooth plateau (no tell-tale acceleration spike). Hardest slip case for detection.
Braking slides with wheel-slide-protection cycling: wheel under-reads by 10-50 % for 0.5-3 s, one or both bogies, no lock.
Wheel lock while braking: the wheel reads ~0 for 0.5-3 s although the tram still moves (a naive estimator declares a stop and loses distance). 40 % of events lock both bogies.
8-15 short gaps of 0.2-2 s on one wheel sensor, both wheel sensors, the controller or all vehicle topics, placed while moving.
Long gaps while moving: both wheel sensors silent for 3-10 s (pure model-based dead reckoning), plus the natural pattern of one sensor silent for 20-75 s starting shortly before a departure.

Bus stalls of 0.5-2 s after which the queued messages are delivered late and drain at 0.9x the nominal period (latency up to 2 s decaying over ~10-20 s) - the exact pattern of real bags. Tests latency handling and use of header stamps vs arrival time.
~1 % of wheel samples corrupted in bursts of 1-3: additive spikes of 5-60 km/h, spurious zeros while moving, sign flips.
NaN, +-inf, absurd codes (6553.5, 1e6, 1e300, -3.4e38...) and negative speeds on the wheels; out-of-range / jumping codes on the controller (127, -128, 100, +-16). The node must not crash.
Stuck sensor while moving: keeps publishing its last value (70 %) or 0 (30 %) with fresh stamps for 2-20 s; one wheel sensor or both.
Degraded sensor: 1-3 km/h white noise + up to 3 % proportional + coloured (AR1, 0.5-2 s) noise on one or both wheel sensors for 1-3 minutes, 2-3 times per run.
Header-stamp jitter (20 ms + 1 % tail of 50-300 ms), arrival jitter 10 ms, 3 % duplicated messages and 1 % out-of-order messages delivered 0.15-0.6 s late on all vehicle topics.

Zero header stamps (0.5 % random + one 2-5 s window), +-1 s stamp glitches on all vehicle topics, and a 20-60 s header-clock offset (+-1 s) drifting at up to 0.1 s/s (as around the 1 s bus gaps of 30618_28538acf / _af7496f0) and ending in a step. Output stamps must stay sane (the judge matches by stamp).
Wheel-diameter errors: front scale drifts linearly to -1..-2 % over the run, rear has a constant +0.5..+2 %. Tests online scale adaptation; position drift grows linearly with distance otherwise.
Controller faults: stuck notch, spurious jumps, invalid codes, +-1..2 encoder offset (4-8 events) plus 3-5 controller dropouts of 0.5-5 s. The model part must not be trusted blindly.
A realistic bad day: a few slips/slides (30 % locks), short dropouts, sparse outliers, mild stamp jitter, 1 % duplicates, +-1 % wheel-scale error.
Stress test - everything at high intensity and GNSS only for 3 s. Success = no crash, no NaN output, bounded error, recovery after each fault.

The kind of synthetic test a jury script would do: rectangular x1.2 over-read on both wheels for 5 s (3x), rectangular -30 % under-read for 2 s (2x), both wheels zeroed for 3 s (1x), both wheel topics cut for 5 s (2x).

Magnitudes as observed in the real bags rather than the 5-30 % design range: low-speed (1-8 m/s) traction slips (requested +30..+90 %, achieved p5/p50/p95 +17/+39/+64 %) lasting 1.5-6 s with cutoff cycles (30618_33bec73f, 30639_50956d6e), braking slides of -30..-70 % and locks (30618_2050d396, 30618_40ffd323), one or both bogies.
